hypothesis: Horizon-specific weighting of the MSE forecast loss reallocates model capacity toward the weakest long-horizon (T+8) predictions, which currently degrade monotonically with lead time, while preserving short-horizon accuracy.
evidence_anchor: Validation shows RMSE worsens monotonically with horizon (T+1 0.0444, T+4 0.0489, T+8 0.0511 on seed43 scratch), indicating the shared MSE under-weights the most difficult long-horizon targets.
expected_effect: T+8 RMSE decreases by at least 5% relative to baseline, while T+1 RMSE increases by no more than 3%.
falsification: If, after training, the weighted average RMSE over all horizons (with weights [1,1,2]) does not improve over the baseline unweighted RMSE by at least 0.5%, or if T+1 RMSE degrades by more than 5% relative to baseline, the trial is refuted.
patch_plan: Modify forecast_loss to accept an optional horizon index (inferred from prediction shape or a new parameter) and apply per-horizon weights. For the chosen weights [1,1,2], multiply the MSE loss for the last horizon (T+8) by 2 while keeping T+1 and T+4 weights at 1. Ensure the loss remains differentiable and finite for masked/virtual runways by applying the same masking logic before weighting.
